entries.resolution: The six final pairs show a fitted brown leather chest beneath the front crossed straps, folded ragged rear garment around the skull pack, visible paired skull cargo, shaped tusked face/hood and a compact jagged rusty cleaver. The initial cloth-only review is superseded by this actual V6 outfit/head/equipment comparison; the hands and complete held cleaver remain clear in front and both profiles.

The rebuilt narrower bodice, long pointed ears, crossed leather front/back harness and actual ankle bone cuffs are visible in the final six pairs. The cuffs wrap the ankle instead of becoming forward boot claws. The ragged leather hem and layered barbed spear are actual geometry, with the held shaft and head moving as one assembly. The render stance is an authored neutral stance rather than a claim to duplicate the original pose exactly.

A single fitted cooking-pot helmet with contacting rim and side handles replaces the generic hood. The bare ogre has one continuous convex forward belly and naturally connected thick arms/legs, rather than a stacked belly sphere. Actual fitted suspenders run over the front and back. One physically hung pan replaces the duplicate pans. The wooden mallet has a rounded solid head with iron end straps and a continuous held handle; all six views show the intended potbelly/cook identity.

The exposed green face now sits under a compact rounded riveted steel cap, with broad pointed ears and short thick legs/boots. A broad continuous curved asymmetrical scrap shoulder shell carries six seated rivets, instead of a thin crescent or generic chest substitute. The fitted brown vest, diamond buckle and riveted loin sheet are visible. The wooden backpack has real board/binding/rivet/crank parts and a cap-height gear; the whole compact rectangular metal hammer leaves the face visible in all six comparisons.

All six original/model pairs show the original hanging green scout beneath the dark bat, separate pink snout/ears and dusty rose scalloped wings. The generic mount was replaced with continuous body/neck, real wing shoulder/elbow/wrist and tarsal/claw anatomy. The whole goblin torso, arms and legs sit within the actual brown suspension harness with tunic/skirt and crossed back straps; physical interfaces are separate measured evidence.

The final six pairs show a large fitted irregular moss shoulder/back canopy, three actual rune stones and visible tan mushroom caps on perimeter stems. A continuous bare green anatomical trunk with thick arms, palms and bare feet replaces the generic booted torso. The held club is a large uneven round stone with moss and a continuous wooden grip, rather than a flat hatchet. The canopy is irregular connected volume rather than evenly aligned collar rods; source organic surface detail remains a geometric estimate.

The crocodile skull now has a visibly projecting long snout, deep open side eye sockets, teeth and stepped rear skull ridges over a physically fitted hood support. The source leaf mantle extends in ragged fitted tiers toward the thighs in front/back/profiles. The barbed spear, exposed orc face and connected limbs remain readable. This resolves the previously opened flat white face-disk and short sparse mantle findings; the final actual six pairs, including both snout profiles, were reopened.

The black ragged hide and cowl now fit the actual back/shoulder anatomy with nonplanar contacting layers; no retained flat detached back plate remains. The blue troll has rebuilt connected thorax/pelvis/limbs, source-specific tusked face, broad curved contacting finger/foot claws and seated cyan crystal details. Ragged leather waist pieces and wrist wraps are visible. The six final source comparisons resolve the initial hide, generic body and sparse gear findings within the geometric reconstruction scope. All six current pairs were reopened after the coherent whole-figure ground seating correction; the source silhouette, held gear and body connections are preserved.

A fitted brown peaked hood and broad lower-face mask, ragged layered brown garment and two actual curved short blades replace the retained shallow source estimates. The lean bodice and connected shoulder/arm surfaces preserve the wide source-inspired stance. Both blades have continuous held hilt/guard/blade assemblies. Front/back/profile comparisons show the source brown masked dust-dancer identity and folded rear tiers without a planar cape or straight generic blades.

The actual rounded steel cap helmet shell has source-sized depth and physically contacting curved ivory horns; the old deep rear slab is gone. The bare continuous ogre body carries a fitted cross harness and angled rough shoulder plates. The mace is a real horned carved skull with recessed eye cavities, a continuous shaft and actual hand grip. The wood shield has separate boards, fitted rim, straps, rear braces and seated rivets. Boss total authored height is retained; all six source pairs show these repairs.

The enlarged horned shoulder skull has real recessed eye sockets and a contacting carrier, while the opposite source salvaged shoulder helmet has a pointed steel relic. The compact cap and metal breast/back plates sit over a fitted brown leather vest; a visible fitted brown rear crossed harness follows the outer plate. The real chain is seated, wrist guards are leather/metal source layers and both inward hooks have complete held grips. All six reopened views resolve the tiny skull, generic outfit and hook-attachment findings.

The giant bronze bell is a real closed-thickness hollow shell with a true irregular front fracture, thick flared lower rim, actual upward-visible underside and purple side/back glyphs. It remains physically seated on the carrier, above a visible small green face and ears. The actual fitted brown vest/loincloth and held stone knocker restore the carrier identity. All six final pairs show the bell opening/crack/rim and improved seated body instead of a smooth opaque gold frustum.

Source-specific red hair is reconstructed as contacting segmented front and rear braids, with a fitted brown leather outfit and real metal/leather armor layers. The axe is a held curved red crescent with a separate dark inner blade, and the waist carries an actual ring. The final six pairs show the braids down the chest/back and the source leather vest silhouette. This recipe is scoped to host13 and preserves the independently frozen mounted host15 braid geometry.

The steel cap has a true rounded shell and contacting rear neck guard rather than a bare green rear head. Fitted riveted steel plates and tassets retain the source armored identity. The dark mirror shield has actual upper spikes, centre mirror relief, seated perimeter rivets and real rear grip/braces/straps. A brown rear crossed harness is physically fitted over the outer rear plate. All six final source pairs show shield and cap identity with attached hands and source orbit mirrors.

All six pairs show the blood bat's dark red body, pink snout, torn red membranes and green red-haired rider. Source red shoulder shells/spikes, brown fitted vest/back straps and forked whole gripped polearm are present. Actual continuous body, real bones/membranes, anatomical hind joints and whole seated upper-body/hips replace disconnected generic forms.

The gold face mask is an angular continuous hollow shell with a pointed lower face, central ridge and real recessed eye openings, rather than black stickers on a flat projecting panel. A fitted dark hood, layered leather jacket, ragged dark front hem, real wrist bracers, amber focus and large gold pouches restore the outfit. The final brown rear X was actually refitted onto the outer jacket/flaps and is now visible in back/profiles. The final six pairs were reopened after that last surface/material repair.

The final troll has a natural connected hunched body, ragged leather hem and contacting ropes/back harness. Three actual carved ivory skulls are seated in a shaped wood carrier rather than cubes floating behind the torso. The held long upward uneven branch club is a whole connected wooden assembly; the former secondary generic weapon replacement was removed so it cannot overwrite this source club. Final front/back/profile pairs show the source totem, fitted carrier and gnarled club identity. All six current pairs were reopened after the coherent whole-figure ground seating correction; the source silhouette, held gear and body connections are preserved.

The tall hood has a tapered pointed front and folded rear profile, seated purple side diamonds and a real broad brown mask covering the lower jaw. Actual upper arms remain exposed green, wrists/forearms have brown leather wraps and shoulders carry charcoal cloth instead of full grey arm plates. A long folded dark cloak carries visible purple rear rune geometry; both held blades are true curved crescents. The six final pairs resolve the retained hood/mask/ornamentation findings and the later independent clothing observations. All six current pairs were reopened after the final genuine middle-station cloth folds; the small contour changes preserve the upper bearing, pointed hood, rear runes and long cloak silhouette.

All six pairs show the grey bloodwolf with separate pointed red brow/cheek/neck harness and dorsal/crupper tack, dark paw claws and bushy curled tail. Brown leather hood/front/rear vest, source red spiked pauldrons/wrist guards and irregular rusty red-edged cleaver replace the prior grey rider/flat pink brow/plain white weapon. Entire rider assembly is inclined over joined seated hips/thighs and source saddle rather than repositioned legs alone.

Broad contacting curved ivory crown ribs replace thin rods/fins. The natural hulking body is covered by an actual fitted dark brown leather front/back vest and dark shoulder caps, with no green punctures through the vest in the final views. The strapped wood/bone carrier, hanging rings, ragged leather skirt and six separately carved ivory staff skulls restore the source equipment. All six final pairs were reopened after the last leather-band repair; boss authored height is preserved. All six current pairs were reopened after the coherent whole-figure ground seating correction; the source silhouette, held gear and body connections are preserved.

A connected articulated bark body and thick gnarled fists are fitted to real palms and limb bearings. Curved branching crown trunks and irregular moss canopy replace the sparse parallel rods. Actual bark/root beard and moss volume wrap the chest/neck, and a long tapered contacting root/moss back mantle reaches toward the thighs instead of stopping as a short bare-backed collar. The six final source/model pairs were reopened after the final root helper export; the prior substantial bark/cloak coverage findings are resolved. All six current pairs were reopened after the coherent whole-figure ground seating correction; the source silhouette, held gear and body connections are preserved.

A rounded fitted steel cap carries true curled ram horns; steel armor and rivets wrap the actual shoulders, wrists and lower body with contacting joints. The final held weapon is a large solid studded cuboid metal hammer on a continuous wooden handle, replacing the wrongly substituted pointed/flanged mace. Actual leather rear harness and ragged waist layers remain. All six final comparisons show the source heavy ram armor and correct hammer class, rather than just inherited weapon metadata.

The source blue soul character has bare cyan feet/hands, layered long ragged blue cloth and a fitted hood. Real shaped ivory skull masks are carried by the wooden fork and the three intentional soul orbits; the centre orbit is above the hood rather than blocking the face. A fitted broad studded brown girdle supports three actual brown-framed hanging cyan diamond seals through contacting links. All six final source comparisons show these visible repairs and the complete held staff assembly.

The pilot has a compact visibly open copper window/cage with thick riveted frame, steel rear plate and actual circular side-bearing housings, iron insets, terminal hubs and seated rivets. Copper limb covers and real mechanical shoulder/elbow/knee/ankle bearing/strut assemblies replace the generic wood/grey body. The gear fist has an actual axle/palm mount connected to its toothed hub and teeth. The final six source pairs show the robust copper pilot identity and circular profile housings; no cosmetic metadata substitute was accepted.

All six source/model pairs show the armored iron bat with dusty rose membranes, fitted metal forehead/cheek/belly and wing-root armor, anatomical hind paws and continuous closed body. The rider has the source rounded steel cap with continuous contacting temples/cheeks, steel front and brown leather rear layers, and the whole wood/metal crossbow held as one connected assembly. The source profile and structural features replace the former generic animal and exposed rider seams. The last source-equipment repair adds a real open leather rear quiver, steel rim bindings, three complete seated arrows with attached heads/fletching and actual measured quiver-to-body and arrow-to-base contacts; the new back gear is visible in final back/side/three-quarter views.

A natural chunky connected green body carries a varied dark rune-rock collar with actual separately seated engraved orange glyphs, instead of a regular unmarked block necklace. The bare abdomen, ragged leather skirt, actual skull belt buckle and asymmetric spiked held mace remain readable. Brown leather forearm/wrist wraps are now actual material/mesh surfaces rather than green skin bands. All six final source pairs show the collar, wraps and source weapon identity.

All six source/model pairs show an ivory skeletal bat with open ribs, vertebral spine, real scapular/pelvic bearings, cyan membranes, separate recessed skull sockets/nasal opening and an open fang-lined jaw. The skeletal rider has the original dark blue hood and fitted dark cloth with pale steel armor, rather than the previous nearly white icy body. Whole seated rider joints, carved skull and held source gear remain joined throughout the native assembly.

All six source/model pairs show the original timber flying chassis: open pilot compartment, plank walls, tan wooden sail wings with wood/iron struts, fitted iron front plate, bronze/leather corner rails and rivets, rear diagonal braces and deep bored side engines. The brown hooded green pilot is crouched within the frame with source ears, leather clothing and whole crossbow. The complete upper body moved with the seated hips and arms; the source compartment and engine depth replace the earlier generic mount.

All six final source/model pairs show the prismatic purple bat with three broad attached turquoise front diamonds at brow/wing roots and the matching broad rear diamond. The final visibility correction moves the real crystal shapes out of the previously buried cranium/wing/back surfaces while preserving physical attachment. The brown hooded green rider has source ears, fitted brown leather clothing and whole short blade; continuous bat body, natural hind joints, wing bones and caudal root resolve the old generic anatomy.

All six final source/model pairs show the large storm-wing bat king with dark continuous body, broad red torn membranes, curved gold temple horns, source forehead armor, red layered chest caparison and physical gold chest chains. The crowned green rider keeps the brown strapped vest, fitted red tiered rear mantle and whole held axe. Complete rider seating and anatomical hind legs/wing roots replace the previous disconnected forms; authored boss height retains the immutable V5 minimum.

The twin-point hood and full ankle-length charcoal robe have real gold facings and front/back seals. The shield has a dark sun face and a conspicuous physically seated gold perimeter, while the whole staff has a brown shaft, gold ring/emblem and hand contact. Both shoulder skull assemblies directly support actual hanging ivory runic tabs down the upper back, visible in back and both profiles after the final relocation. All six final source pairs were reopened, resolving the earlier short robe, grey rim, pale shaft and hidden-tab findings. All six current pairs were reopened after the final genuine middle-station robe folds; the small contour changes preserve the top bearing, gold facings, seals and hanging rear rune tabs.

The rebuilt grey troll carries a curved connected ivory rib cage around a genuinely open recessed chest cage/lantern. The staff has a true bone fork and hanging closed-thickness lantern cage around its intentional cyan soul, with a continuous held shaft. Natural thick limbs/bare feet and a ragged leather waist replace generic boots. The obsolete two flat detached rear baldric planks were removed; the remaining actual diagonal crossed harness follows the back surface. All six final comparisons show the repaired cage and source gear identity. All six current pairs were reopened after the coherent whole-figure ground seating correction; the source silhouette, held gear and body connections are preserved.

The character has bare connected icy blue limbs and a real fitted icy pelvis, a ragged purple hood/shoulder mantle, faceted purple held sword and a visible bright silver waist girdle. Nine real folded trailing ragged purple garment panels extend below the waist toward the calves in back/profiles, replacing the short fan over bare legs. Their roots are physically seated; no flat purple back plate remains. All six final pairs were reopened after the final long-drape export and show the source icy/cloth identity.

All six final source/model pairs show a dark bat with actual hollow ivory mount skull mask, separate real mask eye openings, bone wing leading structures and darker taupe membranes matching the source sails. The hanging green scout has the second distinct carved skull mask, brown hood/body/skirt and physical side packs, whole short weapon and contacting brown suspension harness. Entire suspended upper body, hips and limbs form a joined source assembly rather than displaced boots.

All six final source/model pairs show the eclipse bat's purple body and dusty pink/violet scalloped membranes, source broad open silver crescent wing-root guards, anatomical wing/hind leg interfaces and physical tack. The rider has the deep purple steel cap with continuous contacting temples/cheeks and silver brow/rim, brown leather front/rear vest beneath the silver collar, and a whole purple spear with attached crescent pennant seal. The final source material fix applies to actual exposed fitted plates, so the source brown vest remains visible in front and rear views.

The exposed green face wears an actual broken crown rather than a closed slab helmet. Rough steel upper armor, heavy actual steel thighs/knees/greaves/boots and a short torn red loincloth restore the source knight identity, replacing the long red robe/green legs/brown boots. The dark shield has a deep real split with contacting rear braces and gold crown relief, the sword is a whole held assembly and brown rear X straps visibly fit the outer armor. Final six views show these source repairs.

All six final pairs show the grey-purple rift wolf with shaped snout, recessed eyes, natural canine joints/paws, bushy curled tail, source grey dorsal armor and purple back shards. Its brown strapped rider has the dark hood/ears, source spiked grey shoulder equipment, seated whole body and reins. The final source weapon repair replaces the generic spear head with a real connected forged fork and physically seated purple crystal, visible in front/back/side views.

Prominent pointed ears, a fitted charcoal hood, shaped red lower-face mask and ragged cloth tiers restore the source rogue silhouette. Actual green upper arms stay exposed, brown leather wraps cover the forearms/wrists and charcoal ragged shoulder cloth replaces full hard grey arm guards. The two short knives have source-inspired curved blade/guard/hilt assemblies physically under their held pivots. All six final source pairs show the folded tiers and repaired cloth/skin identity.

All six final pairs show the thunder manta's continuous flattened curved trunk, rolled cephalic front fins, real long recessed mouth, rectangular recessed eyes, broad swept pectoral fins and long tapering stinging tail. The real fitted overlapping dorsal armor has outward positive-Z thickness and raised caps, replacing previously inward/buried relief; source ivory angular wing runes are physically seated on the fin surface. The source red-masked rider keeps a dark hood, brown strapped vest, whole spear/crimson pennant and joined seated body; hidden depth and camera differences remain authored estimates.

All six final pairs show the Hollow Sky King as a true skeletal creature rather than a generic humanoid: real open ribs surrounding the captive green-faced hooded soul and turquoise heart, exposed curved neck/vertebrae, an angular skull with real sockets and open fang-lined lower jaw, swept horn/bone features, grey overlapping back plates and articulated curled armored tail. Source ragged taupe wings and real jointed bone toes are present. Apertures remain physically open and recessed; boss height remains at least the V5 baseline.

The rounded fitted steel cap and contacting rear neck guard replace the oversized rear slab. The shoulders, arms, waist, thighs, greaves and boots carry actual steel armor rather than a brown coat and bare limbs. The shield is a long pointed kite with an actual faceted tinted prism inset, continuous fitted frame, three upper crystals, seated rivets and real rear grip/straps. The spear has one broad faceted diamond head instead of multiple barbs. All six source pairs show the corrected heavy steel/phalanx identity and physical held gear.

All six final pairs show the fire bat with dark body, orange membranes, fitted riveted metal forehead/cheek/belly/wing-root armor, anatomical toes and real wing shoulder/elbow/wrist. The source dark cap has contacting temple/cheek steel and orange rune, with a brown rear vest and crimson pennant. The final physical pike has a real iron diamond blade with attached orange diamond rune in place of the generic gold tip; whole rider and weapon assemblies remain seated and connected.

The ogre has a continuous natural potbelly, source-specific fitted steel cap/visor, rough riveted armor and cuffs. Both actual caged cyan shoulder lanterns have physically contacting mounts and cage pieces. The final weapon is a solid large cuboid studded/spiked metal mallet with a whole wooden held handle, replacing the wrongly substituted rounded/flanged mace. Source bare belly harness and ragged leather waist remain visible. All six final pairs show the repaired armor, lantern and mallet identity.

The face cover has real open recessed eyes, three pointed ivory crown blades and an amber/gold focus. A real long folded dark purple robe carries actual broad orange/gold shoulder mantle facings visible across front/back/profiles, and a continuous orange ragged lower hem follows the real jagged bottom ring. These physical facings replace the ineffective tiny centre accents and two vertical bars alone. The held weapon is a whole long poleaxe with broad curved faceted blade and separate pointed top pike. All six final pairs were reopened after the final mantle/hem repair.

All six final pairs show the two distinct green drummers in brown fitted outfits, steel caps, independent seated hips/thighs and arms, beside the actual timber barrel drum with hide heads, steel hoops/staves, skull motif, straps and four whole gripping mallets. The dark bat has red membranes, source ears/nose, continuous torso, real hind joints and wing bones. The former second drummer head gap and missing second-rider scope were resolved through real cervical/body fitting and both complete measured joint chains.

Continuous actual hollow metal head/body shells enclose real dark recesses rather than an exterior painted diamond. Split dark front breastplates support two actual cyan side gems, while three separate recessed cyan crystals form the central chain; intentional soul volumes stay inside the open armor. Cyan neck and front/back waist seams are visible through genuine openings. Fitted metal hip/skirt/leg armor and the whole contacting sword replace brown garment/generic parts. All six final source pairs show the restored hollow revenant layout.

All six final pairs show the Last Howl wolf's dark continuous body, real natural canine joints/paws, curled shaggy tail, fitted fur flank locks and source ivory canine mask with separate recessed red sockets, carved nasal aperture, swept skull ridges and real jaw teeth. The rider has a rounded steel cap, brown outfit, source axe, two actual outer-surface-fitted brown shaggy mantle layers and a strapped back banner with folded red cloth/black wolf insignia. The final mantle correction removes oversized steel shoulder spikes and stale straight rear straps that occluded the hide; the dark/light brown pointed fur layers are visible from the final back/side/three-quarter views.

All six final pairs show the bat thieves with a dark hood, brown strapped outfit, two short physical daggers, two folded red head-owned scarf streamers and attached gold bells with real open undersides/metal suspension. The source red membranes, purple dark animal body, actual wing roots, toes and fitted source tack replace the generic creature. Scarf roots now follow the whole head assembly and bell supports meet actual thorax surfaces.

The troll has a connected hunched naked stone body with no retained brown tunic/boots, broad actual finger/toe claws and a shaped projecting lower jaw/tusks. The belly is a genuine wide oval carved aperture with dark interior, a recessed cyan soul and separate thick upper/lower curved contacting tooth rows, replacing a flat black panel/triangle teeth. Irregular dark overlapping obsidian back/shoulder/forearm armor replaces a repeated uniform grid. All six final pairs show source maw and stone anatomy identity; the back carapace is armor rather than cloth. All six current pairs were reopened after the coherent whole-figure ground seating correction; the source silhouette, held gear and body connections are preserved.

All six final source/model pairs show Bernhard on the redesigned dark dragon with exactly two canonical hind legs, a tall curved neck with overlapping light steel-grey throat plates, angular plated snout/jaw, recessed amber eyes, three swept horn pairs with amber insets, dark overlapping scales, bronze strapped chest plates, burnt-orange scalloped wings and a long curled armored tail with orange tip. The crouched dark rider has a whole gold-guarded sword with attached orange flame/rune strips, reins and a physical ornate strapped back throne/tower with finials, skull and chain ensemble visible from the rear. Source identity replaces the generic four-legged mount; physical source contacts and authored V5 boss height are retained. After the final metadata-only scope repair, I personally reopened all six newly rendered source/model rows again: the same geometry, charcoal rider cloth, colors, whole sword and source identity remain intact. The physical cloth audit now selects the actual overlapping mantle and skirt meshes while retaining the historical cape record.
